attributes.residual: TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE ACCEPTED CORPUS AND ONE ADDITION, each checkable in one command. (1) UB'S COMPONENT (1) IS REFUTED. UB read fndiff's two IMMEDIATE rows -- T@370 `stw r29,80(r1)` against O@36c `stw r0,108(r1)`, and T@378 `stw r29,104(r1)` against O@374 `stw r29,80(r1)` -- as retail homing a pair at 80/104 where ours homes at 108/80, called it 'the declaration-order lever and the one thing here that is plainly source-shaped', and made it the next lane's step 1. slotdiff reports SLOT MAP IDENTICAL: 33 slots each side, every offset used the same number of times, frame 184 both, saves r29 both. The aligned view shows why the matcher lies -- BOTH streams contain all three stores `stw r0,108(r1)`, `stw r29,80(r1)` and `stw r29,104(r1)`; ours simply issues each one slot LATER against the interleaved `fsubs`/`fmuls` chain, and the matcher then pairs `stw r29,80` against `stw r0,108` across the drift. This is the SAME artifact class UD caught on setup_vmu_entries, now confirmed on a second function in a second TU: read an IMMEDIATE row as 'something non-schedule is here', never as 'this slot is wrong', and settle frame questions with slotdiff. (2) THE PRAGMA LEVER IS DEAD IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. The lane's banked next lever was a scoped `#pragma opt_propagation off`; reading the TU first shows animate_panel_piece (lines 1320-1394) already sits INSIDE an opt_propagation-off region -- `off` at line 417, `reset` at line 1395, which is the line immediately after the function's closing brace -- so the lever was already applied and could not be applied again. Forcing the setting the other way (`on`) returns NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL with object bytes unchanged, which closes the question categorically rather than by inference: this function's codegen does not depend on opt_propagation at all. (3) AN ADDITION UC MISSED. UC classified the function SCHEDULE with `screened_against_target: no`; the aligned view now confirms the schedule label AND finds one word UC's signature does not carry -- `xoris r0,r0,32768` (target) against `xoris r0,r5,32768` (ours) at +0x340. Any postprocessor rule here is therefore permutation PLUS a recolor stage, not a bare permutation. (4) AND THE RULE IS NOT YET SIZEABLE. wf_word_diff.py reports 46 DIFFERING WORDS at 251 instructions. The two windows read this session plus the `xoris` account for roughly twenty of them, so over half the residual is unlocalised and NO window set can be chosen yet. This record was drafted recommending a permutation-plus-recolor rule and the word count withdrew that recommendation before it was proposed -- which is the run-35 gate and the run-37 dispatch rule working exactly as intended: quote the differing WORDS, never the family label, and never size a rule against a cluster count.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: If the full-body walk shows the remaining ~26 words are all pure register-field differences inside otherwise-equal runs -- i.e. one consistent whole-function renaming rather than additional reordering -- then the residual really is permutation-plus-recolor after all and the two-window framing was merely incomplete rather than wrong; run `tools/gdl/regnorm.py game/ui/screensaver animate_panel_piece` and read its STRUCTURAL row count, which the gate baseline currently records as genuine 0, against the aligned view before concluding either way.

YES for what is claimed as measured: slotdiff, fndiff --ops, wf_word_diff and the fnasm --diff aligned view at 0x340:0x3a0 were all run against the objects ninja built this session, and the three shared `stw` words were counted in each stream individually rather than taken from the matcher's pairing. NO for the residual's full extent: 46 words were counted but only about twenty were localised, and the gap is stated here rather than papered over -- the earlier draft of this record recommended a rule on the strength of the un-run word count, and running it is what withdrew the recommendation.
hypothesis.statement: MANDATORY STEP 1 IS A WORD CENSUS, NOT A RULE. animate_panel_piece is schedule-and-recolor class -- 251/251 instructions, identical opcode multiset, identical slot map, identical frame and save set -- but it is NOT yet sized for a postprocessor rule, and this record deliberately withdraws the rule recommendation it was drafted with. wf_word_diff.py reports 46 DIFFERING WORDS; the two windows actually read this session (+0x150..+0x1ac and +0x35c..+0x380) plus the single `xoris` recolor at +0x340 account for roughly twenty, so more than half the residual is somewhere neither this record nor UB nor UC has looked. The next lane must localise all 46 words -- walk `fnasm game/ui/screensaver animate_panel_piece <lo>:<hi> --diff` across the whole 0x0:0x3ec body -- and only then decide the window set. Authoring a permutation over the two known windows would be sizing a rule against a residual that is demonstrably larger than the rule, which is the exact failure claim.law.identical-multiset-is-blind-to-displacements.20260831.v1 and the run-35 word-count gate exist to prevent.
